title: Ankle monitor puts Florida teen at the scene of a $210K Porsche theft, deputies say
comment: Deputies say a 19-year-old joined at least three others in taking a $210,000 Porsche Panamera, seven pairs of shoes included, from a mansion in Miami-Dade's Horse Country. The court-ordered GPS ankle monitor he was already wearing from an earlier police-chase case placed him at the scene.
excerpt: Florida Man's $210K Porsche Theft Allegedly Foiled By One Small Mistake: He Was Wearing A GPS Ankle Monitor BroBible

title: Florida man accused of robbing two banks in a prosthetic 'old man' mask
comment: Federal prosecutors say a 40-year-old St. Petersburg man robbed banks in Largo and St. Petersburg wearing a realistic old-man mask with gray facial hair, and told the tellers to leave out the dye packs. He was on supervised release at the time, having served a decade-long federal sentence for five bank robberies in Texas.
excerpt: Florida man arrested for allegedly robbing bank wearing 'old man' mask, DOJ says firstcoastnews.com

title: Scarborough police round up three escaped alpacas
comment: Scarborough police on patrol found three alpacas wandering Scottow Hill Road and walked them down the street behind a cruiser until the owner could be found. The suspects were returned home without charges.
excerpt: Police officers on patrol in Maine wound up apprehending some unusual suspects: a trio of escaped alpacas.

title: TSA finds Wolverine-style claws in a carry-on at Sea-Tac
comment: TSA officers at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport spotted a three-bladed set of Wolverine-style claws on the X-ray and pulled it out of a carry-on bag. Asked whether anything sharp was packed, the passenger was not sure, then remembered the claws once they were on the table and left them behind.
excerpt: TSA officers find bizarre weapon with ‘Wolverine-style claws, Freddy Krueger blades’ at Seattle airport New York Post

title: A neighbor's appeal over a second horse sends Woodside's equestrian rules back for review
comment: Woodside requires an acre of land for two horses, so a resident on 0.45 acres needed a stable exception for his second horse, and a neighbor appealed it all the way to the town council. The council let both horses stay and asked for easier rules, after hearing that some residents keep renewing horse permits for horses they no longer have.
excerpt: Woodside neighbors' dispute over horse permit inspires town to take new look at its equestrian rules The Almanac

title: FTC and eight states sue Toast over hidden fees and hard-to-cancel plans
comment: The FTC and eight states say restaurant software company Toast advertised hardware and software for $0 a month, then made it back through poorly disclosed fees, pricier card processing and surprise early termination charges for restaurants trying to leave. The complaint also questions the promised round-the-clock support, which owners say was hard to reach at any hour.
excerpt: FTC, states sue Toast over fees, deceptive subscription practices Reuters

title: Acworth HOA fines family $25 a day over its front-yard vegetable garden
comment: An Acworth HOA has fined a family $25 a day since late September over the steel trough beds of peppers, tomatoes and herbs in their front yard, a daily rate reporters could not find in any published fine schedule. The family answered with a Halloween banner mourning the garden, and the board answered by asking the homeowner, one of its own members, to stay away from its meetings.
excerpt: Georgia family puts HOA dispute on Halloween sign as $25-a-day garden fines pile up Yahoo

title: Los Angeles library unveils the world's largest pop-up book
comment: The Los Angeles Public Library marked its centennial with a Guinness-certified pop-up book that opens to 15.41 by 20.01 feet, with scenes rising as high as 11 feet. Turning a single page takes a team of 10 people.
excerpt: The Los Angeles Public Library is celebrating its centennial anniversary by playing host to an unusual tome: the world s largest pop-up book.

title: Villages man accused of taking a hammer to his doctor's Tesla after canceled surgeries
comment: Deputies say a man from The Villages, upset that his doctor had called off two procedures, one of them because he drank water beforehand, put on a surgical mask and hit the doctor's Tesla windshield twice with a hammer. The car's cameras recorded the entire visit, which made the surgical mask the only precaution that did not work.
excerpt: Florida man angry over canceled surgery, smashed doctor's Tesla with hammer, deputies say FOX 35 Orlando

title: Riverside public works employee rescues a child's stuffed cat from a storm drain
comment: A child's stuffed cat fell into a storm drain on the way to school in Riverside, and a public works employee lifted the grate and fished it out with a reaching tool. The city celebrated the rescue online, with the child's mother supplying the photos.
excerpt: A public works employee in an Ohio city is being praised for an unusual rescue involving a stuffed toy that fell into a storm drain.

title: Florida jury convicts man who swallowed $769,500 in stolen Tiffany earrings
comment: Posing as a representative for an Orlando Magic player, a Houston man walked out of the Tiffany store at the Mall at Millenia with four diamond earrings worth $769,500, then tried to swallow them when he was stopped on Interstate 10. An Orange County jury convicted him of robbery and grand theft, and Tiffany took the earrings back after a thorough cleaning.
excerpt: Florida man behind Mall at Millenia’s bizarre jewelry heist found guilty WKMG
